analysis.title: DeskTalk - Warsh keeps December on the table, updates calendar
key_insights: The FOMC left rates unchanged as expected in a 10-2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented in favor of a 25bp rate hike.

The policy statement was largely unchanged. The main change upgraded the description of economic activity from "solid" to "strong". The committee also said the accumulation of more information will help it decide the policy stance.
Chair Warsh said productivity is strong and capital investment remains robust, while inflation remains elevated. He characterized growth as accelerating and broadening.
Warsh said financial conditions have tightened but would not call them "tight". The most dovish point of the event was his remark that most at the Fed do not think the economy is running hot.

Warsh announced a revised FOMC meeting structure for 2027 and 2028. The Committee will still meet eight times a year, but one meeting in 2027 and two in 2028 will be strategy meetings with no policy rate decision.

US rates rallied during the press conference, with front-end yields falling as much as about 10bps before retracing modestly. The broad dollar index softened (DXY -0.25%) and headline equity indices were mostly unchanged.
Citi hosted a FedLive panel at 15:30 ET (19:30 GMT) after the October FOMC press conference, with its US Economist, a US Rates Salesperson and the Head of Equity Trading Strategy.

macro_indicators.reading: Rates unchanged, 10-2 vote, two dissents in favor of a 25bp hike
macro_indicators.interpretation: The hold was expected. The two hawkish dissents show some of the committee leaning toward tightening, while Warsh's press conference comments were read as dovish and front-end yields fell.

macro_indicators.reading: Fell as much as ~10bps during the press conference, then retraced modestly
macro_indicators.interpretation: Markets read Warsh's remarks, especially that most at the Fed do not think the economy is running hot, as less hawkish than the dissents implied.
The dollar softened as US rates rallied.

risk_factors: Inflation remains elevated per Warsh, and two voters dissented in favor of a hike, so a December hike stays possible.
Growth is described as accelerating and broadening, which could keep upward pressure on inflation and rates.
